```{r}
#| label: setup
#| include: false

# ── What this file is ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────
#
# A Quarto document whose *engine is knitr*, which is what makes it R rather
# than Python. Toft reads the engine in detection, in this order:
#
#   1. [notebook] engine = "knitr" in toft.toml
#   2. engine: / knitr: in this YAML header
#   3. a fenced ```{r} chunk
#   4. otherwise `notebook` in the Python family
#
# This file declares it in the header *and* is full of {r} chunks, so it is
# unambiguous by two of the four rules.
#
# It is rendered **once, at build time**, with this app's own environment, and
# what is served is the directory that fell out. There is no R process behind
# the page a viewer loads. That is the sharpest edge of the framework and it is
# worth saying plainly: whatever a chunk prints is in the published document,
# and on a public app "published" means the internet.
#
# Quarto is not bundled with Toft. On an install without it, this app fails
# to deploy naming QUARTO_BIN rather than being quietly rendered with nbconvert.

knitr::opts_chunk$set(comment = "#>", collapse = TRUE)

# The house palette, so a base-R plot matches every other example in the
# gallery. Five series and no sixth; the tone colours are Toft's own.
LP <- list(
  ink   = "#14161C", ink2 = "#5A5F6B", ink3 = "#8A8F9B",
  rule  = "#E5E6EA", paper = "#FAFAFB",
  c1 = "#4338CA", c2 = "#0E9AA7", c3 = "#2E9E63", c4 = "#8B5CF6", c5 = "#C2703B",
  ok = "#10B981", att = "#F59E0B", dan = "#EF4444", info = "#3B82F6"
)

# One plotting frame for the whole document. Base R draws a box and tick marks
# by default, and both are noise next to a horizontal grid.
frame <- function(ylim, xlim, xlab = "", ylab = "", grid_n = 5,
                  mar = c(3.4, 4.4, 0.6, 0.8), grid = "h") {
  par(mar = mar, family = "sans", las = 1,
      col.axis = LP$ink2, col.lab = LP$ink2, fg = LP$rule, cex.axis = 0.86,
      cex.lab = 0.86, tcl = -0.25, mgp = c(2.6, 0.5, 0))
  plot(NA, xlim = xlim, ylim = ylim, xlab = xlab, ylab = ylab, axes = FALSE)
  # The grid goes behind the bars and runs across whichever axis carries the
  # measurement: horizontal for a column chart, vertical for a bar chart lying
  # on its side. One argument, because a chart with the grid on the wrong axis
  # is a chart nobody can read a value off.
  if (grid == "h") {
    at <- pretty(ylim, grid_n)
    abline(h = at, col = LP$rule, lwd = 1)
    axis(2, at = at, col = NA, col.ticks = NA, line = -0.6)
  } else {
    abline(v = pretty(xlim, grid_n), col = LP$rule, lwd = 1)
  }
}

pct <- function(x, d = 2) sprintf(paste0("%.", d, "f%%"), x)
hm  <- function(mins) sprintf("%dh %02dm", mins %/% 60, round(mins %% 60))

# Emit raw HTML from an `asis` chunk.
#
# The indentation below is for whoever reads this file; pandoc reads a line
# indented four spaces as a code block, which is how a masthead ends up on the
# page as source. So the indentation is stripped on the way out, and the block
# is fenced as raw HTML so no part of it is re-parsed as Markdown.
html_block <- function(x) {
  cat("\n```{=html}\n")
  cat(gsub("(?m)^[ \\t]+", "", x, perl = TRUE))
  cat("\n```\n\n")
}
```

```{r}
#| label: read
#| include: false

# A missing file is a first-class outcome rather than a crash. A build that dies
# with "cannot open file" makes somebody read a build log to find out a nightly
# export did not land; a report that says so on its own front page does not.
data_dir  <- if (nzchar(Sys.getenv("REVIEW_DATA_DIR"))) Sys.getenv("REVIEW_DATA_DIR") else "data"
inc_file  <- file.path(data_dir, "incidents.csv")
svc_file  <- file.path(data_dir, "services.csv")
have_data <- file.exists(inc_file) && file.exists(svc_file)

if (have_data) {
  inc <- utils::read.csv(inc_file, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
  svc <- utils::read.csv(svc_file, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
  inc$opened <- as.POSIXct(inc$opened, tz = "UTC")
  inc$week   <- as.integer(format(inc$opened, "%V"))
  inc$day    <- as.Date(inc$opened)
} else {
  inc <- data.frame(); svc <- data.frame()
}

# The quarter, in minutes, which is the denominator every availability figure
# below divides by. Stated once so the numbers cannot disagree.
QUARTER_DAYS <- 91
QUARTER_MINS <- QUARTER_DAYS * 24 * 60

quarter_label <- "1 April – 30 June 2026"
```

```{r}
#| label: not-there
#| echo: false
#| results: asis

if (!have_data) {
  cat(sprintf(
    ':::{.callout-important}\n## The export did not land\n\n`%s` and `%s` are what this review reads, and at least one of them is not there. Everything below would be an empty table, so it is not rendered.\n\nThe deploy **succeeded** — this is a report about missing data, not a broken build.\n:::\n',
    inc_file, svc_file))
  knitr::knit_exit()
}
```

```{r}
#| label: masthead
#| echo: false
#| results: asis

slug <- Sys.getenv("TOFT_APP_SLUG", "")
mode <- Sys.getenv("TOFT_EXECUTION_MODE", "")
on_platform <- nzchar(Sys.getenv("TOFT_APP_TOKEN"))

cap <- function(label, on, note = "") sprintf(
  '<span class="cap %s" title="%s"><b>%s</b></span>',
  if (on) "on" else "off", note, label)

html_block(sprintf('
<div class="lp-block">
  <header class="masthead">
    <div class="masthead-in">
      <div>
        <div class="wordmark">
          <span class="mark" aria-hidden="true"></span>
          <span class="wordmark-text">Toft example</span>
        </div>
        <h1>Service Review</h1>
        <p class="standfirst">Ten services, %d incidents and one quarter, rendered once at
           deploy time and served as the document that fell out.</p>
      </div>
      <div class="masthead-aside">
        <span class="chip chip-lang">R &middot; Quarto (knitr)</span>
        <span class="chip">%s</span>
      </div>
    </div>
  </header>
  <div class="rail"><div class="rail-in">
    <span class="rail-label">Toft</span>%s
  </div></div>
</div>',
  nrow(inc),
  quarter_label,
  paste0(
    cap("Quarto", TRUE, "Rendered with the knitr engine, once, at build time."),
    cap("Built at deploy", TRUE, "Nothing is re-rendered by a restart."),
    cap("R", TRUE, sprintf("%s.%s", R.version$major, R.version$minor)),
    cap("renv.lock", file.exists("renv.lock"),
        "Committed, so the Dependencies tab can enumerate this app."),
    cap("Workload", on_platform,
        if (on_platform) sprintf("Running as a Toft workload (%s mode).", mode)
        else "Rendered outside Toft."),
    collapse = "")))
```

# What happened this quarter {#sec-summary}

```{r}
#| label: headline
#| echo: false
#| results: asis

total_down <- sum(inc$minutes)
s1 <- sum(inc$severity == "S1")
mttr <- mean(inc$minutes)
mttd <- mean(inc$detect_minutes)
change_rate <- mean(inc$change_related == "yes")

tile <- function(k, v, n, tone = "") sprintf(
  '<div class="tile %s"><div class="tile-k">%s</div><div class="tile-v">%s</div><div class="tile-n">%s</div></div>',
  tone, k, v, n)

html_block(sprintf('<div class="lp-block"><div class="tiles">%s</div></div>',
  paste0(
    tile("Incidents", format(nrow(inc), big.mark = ","),
         sprintf("%d severity 1", s1), if (s1 > 6) "tone-att" else "tone-ok"),
    tile("Time lost", hm(total_down),
         sprintf("across %d services", length(unique(inc$service))), "tone-neu"),
    tile("Mean time to restore", hm(mttr),
         sprintf("detected in %s", hm(mttd)), "tone-info"),
    tile("Change-related", pct(change_rate * 100, 0),
         "of all incidents", if (change_rate > 0.3) "tone-dan" else "tone-att"),
    collapse = "")))
```

::: {.callout-note}
## The one number to argue with

`r pct(change_rate * 100, 0)` of this quarter's incidents followed a change.
That is the figure worth taking to a planning meeting, because it is the only
one on this page anybody in the room can do something about before the next
quarter starts. Everything else here describes what already happened.
:::

## Availability against target {#sec-availability}

Availability is downtime over the quarter, and the quarter is
`r format(QUARTER_MINS, big.mark = ",")` minutes. Stated once, in the setup
chunk, so nothing below can quietly divide by something else.

```{r}
#| label: tbl-availability
#| tbl-cap: "Every service, its target, and what it actually did. Sorted by how far short it fell."
#| echo: false

by_svc <- aggregate(cbind(minutes, id = seq_len(nrow(inc)) * 0 + 1) ~ service,
                    data = inc, FUN = sum)
names(by_svc) <- c("service", "down", "count")
tbl <- merge(svc, by_svc, by = "service", all.x = TRUE)
tbl$down[is.na(tbl$down)] <- 0
tbl$count[is.na(tbl$count)] <- 0
tbl$actual <- 100 * (1 - tbl$down / QUARTER_MINS)
tbl$gap <- tbl$actual - tbl$target_pct
tbl <- tbl[order(tbl$gap), ]

out <- data.frame(
  Service = tbl$service,
  Tier = tbl$tier,
  Owner = tbl$owner,
  Incidents = tbl$count,
  Downtime = vapply(tbl$down, hm, character(1)),
  Target = pct(tbl$target_pct),
  Actual = pct(tbl$actual),
  Verdict = ifelse(tbl$gap >= 0, "met", sprintf("short by %s", pct(-tbl$gap))),
  check.names = FALSE
)
knitr::kable(out, align = c("l", "l", "l", "r", "r", "r", "r", "l"))
```

```{r}
#| label: fig-availability
#| fig-cap: "The same table as a picture. The bar is what the service did; the mark is what it promised."
#| echo: true

t2 <- tbl[order(tbl$actual), ]
# The left margin is nine lines because "Customer portal" is the longest name
# in the estate and the default clips it.
frame(ylim = c(0, nrow(t2) + 1),
      xlim = c(min(c(t2$actual, t2$target_pct)) - 0.15, 100.02),
      mar = c(3.4, 9.2, 0.6, 0.8), grid = "v")
tone <- ifelse(t2$gap >= 0, LP$ok, LP$dan)
segments(x0 = par("usr")[1], x1 = t2$actual, y0 = seq_len(nrow(t2)),
         col = tone, lwd = 9, lend = 1)
points(t2$target_pct, seq_len(nrow(t2)), pch = "|", cex = 1.5, col = LP$ink)
axis(2, at = seq_len(nrow(t2)), labels = t2$service, col = NA, col.ticks = NA,
     cex.axis = 0.8, line = -0.6)
axis(1, col = NA, col.ticks = NA, line = -0.8)
mtext("Availability, per cent of the quarter", side = 1, line = 2,
      col = LP$ink2, cex = 0.86)
```

@fig-availability and @tbl-availability are the same nine numbers twice, which
is deliberate: the chart is what somebody looks at, and the table is what they
paste into the follow-up email. Quarto's cross-references mean neither can be
renumbered by hand into disagreeing with the other.

# Where the time went {#sec-causes}

::: {.panel-tabset}

## By cause

```{r}
#| label: fig-cause
#| fig-cap: "Incident count by root cause. Change is the largest bar in most quarters and in most organisations."

by_cause <- sort(table(inc$cause))
frame(ylim = c(0.4, length(by_cause) + 0.6), xlim = c(0, max(by_cause) * 1.08),
      mar = c(3.4, 8.2, 0.6, 0.8), grid = "v")
barplot(as.numeric(by_cause), horiz = TRUE, add = TRUE, axes = FALSE,
        col = LP$c1, border = NA, space = 0.55, width = 0.62)
axis(2, at = seq_along(by_cause), labels = names(by_cause), col = NA,
     col.ticks = NA, cex.axis = 0.86, line = -0.6)
axis(1, col = NA, col.ticks = NA, line = -0.8)
text(as.numeric(by_cause), seq_along(by_cause), labels = as.numeric(by_cause),
     pos = 4, col = LP$ink2, cex = 0.8, offset = 0.4)
```

## By severity, over time

```{r}
#| label: fig-weekly
#| fig-cap: "Incidents a week, split by severity. Thirteen weeks; the quarter starts on the left."

wk <- sort(unique(inc$week))
mat <- sapply(c("S1", "S2", "S3"), function(s)
  as.numeric(table(factor(inc$week[inc$severity == s], levels = wk))))
frame(ylim = c(0, max(rowSums(mat)) * 1.15), xlim = c(0.5, length(wk) + 0.5))
barplot(t(mat), add = TRUE, axes = FALSE, border = NA, space = 0.35,
        col = c(LP$dan, LP$att, LP$c1), width = 0.74)
axis(1, at = seq_along(wk), labels = wk, col = NA, col.ticks = NA,
     cex.axis = 0.75, line = -0.8)
mtext("ISO week", side = 1, line = 2, col = LP$ink2, cex = 0.86)
legend("topright", legend = c("S1", "S2", "S3"), fill = c(LP$dan, LP$att, LP$c1),
       border = NA, bty = "n", horiz = TRUE, cex = 0.82, text.col = LP$ink2)
```

## By region

```{r}
#| label: tbl-region
#| tbl-cap: "Regions, with mean time to restore. A region with few incidents and a long MTTR is a staffing question, not a reliability one."

reg <- do.call(rbind, lapply(split(inc, inc$region), function(d) data.frame(
  Region = d$region[1],
  Incidents = nrow(d),
  S1 = sum(d$severity == "S1"),
  Downtime = hm(sum(d$minutes)),
  MTTR = hm(mean(d$minutes)),
  MTTD = hm(mean(d$detect_minutes)),
  check.names = FALSE)))
knitr::kable(reg[order(-reg$Incidents), ], row.names = FALSE,
             align = c("l", "r", "r", "r", "r", "r"))
```

:::

## Detection is most of restoration {#sec-detection}

```{r}
#| label: fig-detect
#| fig-cap: "Every incident: how long it took to notice against how long it took to fix. Both axes are logarithmic, because the range is three orders of magnitude and a linear plot would be one dot and a cloud."

frame(ylim = log10(range(inc$minutes)), xlim = log10(range(inc$detect_minutes)))
cols <- c(S1 = LP$dan, S2 = LP$att, S3 = LP$c1)
points(log10(inc$detect_minutes), log10(inc$minutes),
       pch = 19, cex = 0.9, col = adjustcolor(cols[inc$severity], alpha.f = 0.62))
ticks <- c(1, 3, 10, 30, 100, 300, 1000)
axis(1, at = log10(ticks), labels = ticks, col = NA, col.ticks = NA, line = -0.8)
axis(2, at = log10(ticks), labels = ticks, col = NA, col.ticks = NA, line = -0.6)
mtext("Minutes to detect", side = 1, line = 2, col = LP$ink2, cex = 0.86)
mtext("Minutes to restore", side = 2, line = 2.8, col = LP$ink2, cex = 0.86,
      las = 0)
legend("bottomright", legend = names(cols), col = cols, pch = 19, bty = "n",
       horiz = TRUE, cex = 0.82, text.col = LP$ink2)
```

Detection is `r pct(100 * mttd / mttr, 0)` of mean restoration time across the
quarter. That ratio is usually the cheapest thing on this page to improve, and
it is the argument for spending on alerting before spending on redundancy.

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true"}
## The arithmetic, if you want to check it

```{r}
#| label: arithmetic
#| echo: true

c(incidents = nrow(inc),
  quarter_minutes = QUARTER_MINS,
  total_downtime = sum(inc$minutes),
  mean_restore = round(mean(inc$minutes), 1),
  mean_detect = round(mean(inc$detect_minutes), 1),
  worst_service = which.max(tapply(inc$minutes, inc$service, sum)))
```

# What Toft did with this file {#sec-platform}

```{r}
#| label: platform
#| echo: false
#| results: asis

kv <- function(k, v) sprintf("<dt>%s</dt><dd>%s</dd>", k, v)

html_block(sprintf('
<div class="lp-block">
  <div class="cards">
    <div class="card">
      <div class="card-hd"><h2>This render</h2></div>
      <div class="card-bd"><dl class="kv">%s</dl></div>
      <div class="card-ft">Nothing is re-rendered by a restart. A wake, a crash restore or a
        repair serves the document this release was deployed with; only a deploy produces a
        new one.</div>
    </div>
    <div class="card">
      <div class="card-hd"><h2>The sharp edge</h2></div>
      <div class="card-bd">
        <div class="note tone-att"><strong>The chunks ran with this app&rsquo;s whole
          environment.</strong> Whatever they printed is in this document, and nothing is
          redacted &mdash; the platform cannot know which cell output is a secret. On a
          public app, &ldquo;published&rdquo; means the internet. The build log lists the
          variable <em>names</em> that were exported, never their values.</div>
        <div class="note"><strong>Quarto is not bundled.</strong> On an install without it,
          a <code>.qmd</code> fails the deploy naming <code>QUARTO_BIN</code> &mdash;
          refused, never quietly rendered with the other engine.</div>
      </div>
    </div>
  </div>
</div>',
  paste0(
    kv("Engine", "<span class=\"badge tone-brand\">knitr</span> &mdash; declared in the YAML header and confirmed by the {r} chunks"),
    kv("R", sprintf("<span class=\"mono small\">%s</span>", R.version.string)),
    kv("Quarto", sprintf("<span class=\"mono small\">%s</span>",
                         Sys.getenv("QUARTO_VERSION", "resolved at build time"))),
    kv("Rendered", format(Sys.time(), "%Y-%m-%d %H:%M %Z")),
    kv("Served from", "<code>toft-render/</code> &mdash; the platform&rsquo;s directory, never the release"),
    kv("Published", "the render, and nothing else: the <code>.qmd</code>, <code>renv.lock</code> and <code>data/</code> are all 404"),
    kv("Packages", sprintf("%d, from <code>renv.lock</code>", {
      lk <- tryCatch(length(jsonlite::fromJSON("renv.lock")$Packages), error = function(e) NA)
      if (is.na(lk)) 0L else lk
    })),
    collapse = "")))
```
